title: Coverage and coexactness in checkerboard slice observations
abstract: We study original-channel rectangular means for a finite checkerboard gradient energy. Permutation cut diagonals yield an explicit logarithmic coercivity bound and finite penalty. Arbitrary cuts exclude exactly strong-null invisible fields, yet sufficiently low coverage admits a real nonzero actual coexact invisible field below the target energy at an explicitly enormous dyadic threshold. A contrast-uniform factor-four coexact projection bound coexists with loss of mean zeros, and a correction-only cost is quantified. Historical priority, matching rates and the nonlinear permutation target remain open. These finite analytical results are not a physical Yang--Mills gap theorem.
